o1.biggest_strength: Crystal-clear diagnosis that isolates Meta as the cost problem and linen as the product leak, with a simple $94 payback rule and a tight ranked move list an owner can act on Monday.
o1.biggest_mistake: No overall contribution-margin figure or baseline, so the board's actual ask (contribution margin up this year) is tracked only as a vague 'up every month' rather than a real number and target.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the baseline and day-90 target for contribution margin as a percent of revenue, and size each move in dollars or points of margin so the ranking can be checked.

o2.biggest_strength: Translates everything into points of contribution margin with explicit low/likely/high ranges, and gives the owner a real baseline (7.8% to 13.6%) plus a day-90 target and per-move sizing, including a bold swatch-kit test.
o2.biggest_mistake: Buries and over-models the numbers: the contribution derivation rests on unstated-but-load-bearing assumptions (order values flat, email mix), the 'at least $94' repeat value is undercounted, and the density of points-of-margin math makes it harder to skim than the plan it is replacing.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Lead with one plain contribution-margin line and slide the point-level math to an appendix, fix the repeat-value phrasing, and simplify the presentation so a non-expert can read it in five minutes.

reason: Both are usable and both nail the Meta-plus-linen-plus-email story, but option 2 gives me a real contribution-margin baseline and target and sizes every move, which is what my board actually asked for; option 1 is cleaner to read but does not put a number on the goal.
